messages:
sarah: incident-bot paged: anomalous KV cache growth on runtime pool 'dedicated-g2' at 21:02 UTC. CPU and GPU queues spiking, tail latency >2s for text-gen routes.

incident-bot: Pager: SEV-2 - kv-cache size growth > 10x baseline, continuous-batching backlog increasing, estimated 11% increased p99 token latency.

mike: seeing large numbers of 'cache divergence detected' logs in the spec-decode pipeline. looks like speculative decoding is creating many ephemeral drafts that populate KV prefixes then never resolve to targets -> cache churn.

leila: confirmed. from traces: sequence of speculative drafts with slightly different prefixes are creating many unique KV keys. continuous-batching groups these into large batches and we get a cascade.

jordan: quick ask - any customer visible errors? emily-cs?

emily-cs: We have a support ticket from AcmeCorp reporting slow responses and occasional timeouts on chat completions. They report timeouts since ~20:50 UTC.

mike: attaching tail of logs:
```
[20:58:42] spec-decode: draft_id=abc123 prefix_hash=0x9f1e entries=384
[20:58:42] kvcache: insert latency spike 120ms key_count=384
[20:58:43] batcher: queued 472 requests, window_ms=12
[20:58:43] runtime: p99=2100ms errors=1.2% (timeouts)
```

leila: initial mitigation idea: reduce continuous-batching window to minimize batch amplification, and increase KV cache eviction aggression for speculative prefixes. quick hotfix could be pushing batch window from 12ms -> 3ms and set speculative key TTL to 2s.

sarah: agree. also we should temporarily disable speculative writeback for drafts (i.e., don't write speculative drafts into the shared KV namespace) until we stabilize. that prevents divergence.

mike: I can push a scoped config change to runtime via canary. plan: 1) deploy batch window = 3ms to 10% of dedicated-g2 nodes; 2) set spec_writeback=false for that canary; 3) observe p99 and cache size.

jordan: what's the rollback plan if canary fails?

mike: deploy-bot will auto-rollback if tail latency increases >5% vs baseline for >5m. also manual rollback: patch config to previous values.

sarah: do we want to notify customers? Emily, coord with support: message template with cause: transient speculative decoding interactions causing cache churn, mitigation in progress.

emily-cs: drafting message: "We're investigating increased latency on chat completions; engineers are deploying a mitigation now to reduce batching window and disable speculative KV writes. Will follow up with ETA." sending to AcmeCorp now.

incident-bot: action required: oncall handoff in 45m. current assignee: sarah. next oncall: mike.

mike: canary deployment started to 10% nodes. pushing config patch:
```
PATCH /config/runtime
{
  "continuous_batch_window_ms": 3,
  "speculative_writeback": false,
  "speculative_prefix_ttl_s": 2
}
```

deploy-bot: Canary started: rollout_id=rl-2026-03-14-008, target=dedicated-g2, fraction=0.10

leila: monitoring dashboards: KV cache unique keys metric dropping after ~90s post-canary. p99 latency trending down from 2100ms -> 580ms on canary hosts.

mike: expanding to 35% after 5m stable.

deploy-bot: Rollout updated: fraction=0.35

sarah: observed overall tail latency reduced to ~670ms across the pool, error rate back to baseline. AcmeCorp confirms improved response times.

emily-cs: AcmeCorp update: "noticed recovery around 21:15 UTC, service more responsive, thanks."

jordan: root cause hypothesis: speculative decoding produced many ephemeral drafts with slightly varying token prefixes; because system was configured to write drafts into shared KV with long TTLs, continuous batching aggregated these writes causing massive cache insertion pressure and unexpected memory growth -> perf cliff.

leila: long-term mitigations proposed: 1) default speculative writeback to isolated per-request namespace (avoid global eviction pressure), 2) adaptive batching (throttle batch window if KV insert rate spikes), 3) detect 'speculative storm' and auto-disable writeback + shrink batch window.

mike: also add guardrails: cap per-request speculative keys written per-sequence, and lower default TTL for speculative keys.

sarah: for the handoff: checklist for next oncall (mike):
- monitor kv_unique_keys and batch_queue_length
- keep speculative_writeback disabled until we've validated refactor
- follow up with infra/research to implement per-request isolation by EOD+3
- update postmortem and customer comms

mike: ack. I'll pick this up for the 00:00 UTC handoff.

incident-bot: Handoff scheduled. New assignee: mike at 22:00 UTC.

sarah: adding quick notes to global incident doc: "Speculative decoding x continuous batching caused cache blowup; hotfix reduced batch window and disabled speculative writeback; customer impact limited to elevated latency/timeouts for a small set of customers between 20:50-21:20 UTC; mitigated via canary and expanded rollout; next steps: implement isolation and adaptive throttles."

emily-cs: closing support ticket pending postmortem. customer satisfied with update.

jordan: any immediate PRs to track? mike/leila please link.

mike: opened PR#3421 - runtime: add spec_writeback toggle and batch_window config.

leila: opened follow-up issue #5592 - kv isolation + adaptive-batching roadmap.

sarah: thanks team. leaving detailed handoff message to mike.

mike: leaving note: will keep speculative_writeback=false until we ship isolation. will follow up in eng-runtime channel tomorrow with design.

incident-bot: Incident state changed -> mitigated (SEV-2 -> MONITORING).
